contexts.text: It is the first flower of love which... conjoins the minds of the consorts.
Their mind was continually in (longing for the goods of others).
With a mind to meet those...
The punishers had a mind to kill them...
The animus of hatred then shines forth...
Who keep the mind in the historical context.
Over head are those who breathe high things with an elate mind.
Not with a deliberate intention...
They at once know the quality of another's mind...
That they captivated the mind. Signified.
The things which are of the mind, or of the affection of knowing and learning.
Keeps his mind in the sense of the things, and not in the words...
They expressed the sense of their mind by changes induced on my face.
When they were communicating the interior sense of their mind...
See Mind. HH 30. DP 324:3. TCR 32:2.
(When) not so remote from charity, their minds are move flexible.
This opinion... possessed the minds of the most instructed.
Preface [2]. Would strengthen his mind in the negative.
The Spirits keep his mind fixedly in the thought...
Those who are in infirmity of mind...
An immission thus into the minds of others.
All the interior affections of the lower mind and of the mind are expressed by the face.
Is easily distinguished from cheerfulness of mind...
They who breathe such things in the mind...
He had such a disposition to command others.
Historicals detain the lower mind in themselves; and thus draw away the mind from thinking...
Some who had been of infantile mind... appear to themselves in white.
The animus of that affection. Signified.
To run = propensity or animus.
By the sense of his mind he can express...
If he has learned to simulate, he assumes as it were another lower mind... for it is the lower mind which appears in the face... He is affected... by the mind which thus shines from the countenance.
Perception... concerning the animus of natural good then. Signified.
The animus of inverting the state and of depriving truth of life from itself. Signified.
This animus lies deeply hidden...
The outermost affections are those which are of the body... those next interior are of the lower mind, and are called natural affections...
That he has known animus and power. Signified.
That to know the quality is to know the animus, is evident.
Those who have been of discordant mind are dissociated.
His sphere manifests the quality of his mind; that is, the quality of his will and thought.
Afterwards (in conjugial love) comes conjunction of minds, in that the one wills as the other...

There is a correspondence of the internals with all things of the face; hence the lower mind shines forth from the countenance; and the interior mind or mind, from the eyes... Gladness of the lower mind and joy of the mind produce singing...
All things of the body represent those of the lower mind and of the mind.
The thoughts and affections are the interiors, because they are of the lower mind and mind.
This delight (in seeing) is not of the eye; but is of the lower mind and its affection.

The influx from the cerebellum insinuates itself especially into the face; as may be evident from the fact that the mind is inscribed on the face... so that from the face another knows what affections he has, and what are the changes of his lower mind and mind.
If his mind were to inhere in these things while he is dancing...
They hide this disposition.
The mind to procure for themselves truths through scientifics. Signified.
When he is of a cheerful mind... his food nourishes better.
The mind to procure good for truths. Signified.
To descend = the mind, or intention.
They consociate with themselves such as agree in minds.
That it would not enter into their mind. Signified.
Thus, by the face is signified the mind.
When the cupidity of dominating... invaded the mind...
The appearance of everyone there is according to his mind and life.
Marriages... are conjunctions of lower minds and of minds.
Legitimate conjunction takes places when the minds are conjoined; and... no conjunction... when the minds are disjoined.
Legitimate conjunction, which is that of minds, takes place when both are of like good and truth...
Worship from a grateful mind... Signified.
This error is seated in many minds...
For all things which are of the mind are presented in some natural shape in the body...
When a youth sees one to whom his mind draws him...
From their faces they see whether they agree in minds; for the face of everyone there is the index of the mind.
Beauty, etc., affect both the senses and the minds.
Hence the face is called the index of the mind.
How it compares with that rest of mind possessed by those who are content in God.
The cupidities into which their lower mind is carried.
The grief of mind... which is called melancholy.
When this is seated in one's mind... in the same proportion he is led by the Lord.
The infants who die... are of a like infantile mind...
By games suitable to the minds of the infants.
Because thus he can remove his mind from an idle life.
The rich who have rejected the things of Heaven and the Church from the mind are in Hell.
The body... is the external form corresponding to the internal form which is of his lower mind and mind.
The essential of marriage is the unition of the minds or of the minds. Hence, such as are the minds or minds in themselves, such is the unition. (Continued. See Mind.)
Whence man has interior activities serviceable to the operations of his mind...
As they were of diverse minds... after a short time they were disjoined.
They then see each other no longer... unless they are of a like mind from a like love.
For the face is the image of everyone's mind.
In the first state of man after death... he is of like mind...
When anything arises which he knows to be insincere... and to which his mind is carried...
The elation of mind in externals which is called pride.
His mind would become torpid.
Celebrated in the minds of others.
The interiors which are of the mind... are turned to that which he loves above all things; and the exteriors which are of the lower mind are turned to where the interiors are turned.
As many men, so many faces, and so many minds.
Innumerable parts constitute the body; and innumerable affections constitute the mind.
Serve for captivating minds.

No one is reformed in a state of sickness of mind; because sickness of mind takes away rationality... for the mind is sick and not sound; and a sound mind is rational, but not a sick mind. Such sicknesses are... griefs of mind from misfortunes, anxieties and anguish of mind from a vitiated state of the body...
As he sees the mind of another from his face.
A motion of the mind with many in the Church to receive the doctrine. Signified.
There are many causes which conjoin lower minds, but not souls...
The first external cause of cold is a dissimilitude of lower minds and manners.

But external similitudes and dissimilitudes are not of souls, but of lower minds. By lower minds are meant the external affections and derivative inclinations... For we say, Have I a mind to do this or that? by which is perceived the affection and inclination to it. The persuasions taken up concerning this or that kind of life are also wont to form these lower minds...
As the soul is the man himself... it is evident whence it is that the mind, the lower mind, the nature, the inclination, and the affection of the father's love dwell in offspring after offspring...

In every work which proceeds from man, there is the whole man such as he is as to the mind, or such as he is essentially. By the mind is meant his affection of love and the derivative thought. These form his nature; in general, his life.
The phantasy of this love carries their minds away...
Which exhilarated the mind of everyone...
As by their... feasts such consociations of minds were signified...
Sons are born into a general likeness of their parents as to... minds.
You might thus be convinced of the likeness of lower minds and minds.
When anyone is revolving evil in the mind, and intending it...
So draw away their mind, and alienate them from Christianity.
The lower or natural mind, commonly called the animus...
The third of man's faculties in succession is the natural mind, or animus. (See Mind, and at WE 653.)

These Genii correspond completely to that power in man which has been called above the lower mind, or animus. It is the nature of these Genii that they there excite those affections which are called the passions of the lower mind...

To animals a certain mind has been given which is called the animus; from which they are called animals; and the like is also given to man, which has been called by us above the natural mind; but in order that it might be of service to his intellectual mind...
And the natural mind itself, or animus...
The passions of the lower mind; thus the properly animal life...
Cupidities, which are longings in the natural mind; from which this mind is called the animus; and these cupidities, the cupidities of the animus.

To these succeed again infra-celestial goodnesses, which are middle ones between the spiritual and the natural ones, and properly affect the natural mind, or animus, which men have in common with animals.
To these succeed the evils which properly touch the lower mind, or animus...
(These mice, etc.) are formed according to... the purpose for the sake of which they are misers.
Nor can a man's lower mind be torn to pieces without perishing, because it coheres with the body.
With a mind to persevere.
Whether he (acknowledged this) from his mind, I do not yet know.
They retain in mind the companions they had had in the life of the body.
With a mind to chastise.
Speech and persuasions have no effect when the mind desires, or is affected with love. Explained.
Others who have a like animus...
Has the mind intent on wealth.
There was his mind...
That the Angels can examine the mind of a man separated as it were from the man. Explained.
What he had had, or had intended, in the mind.
a. How the minds of the inhabitants in this world are in common. Explained.
The mind is Known (from their speech).
It came into my mind that...
The mind, or the affections of the man, appear inscribed on the face.
Men not only as to the mind and memory, but also as to sense.
Until such a disposition ceases.
Their deceitful disposition.
Keeping the mind in these things, and thus driving to them.
Similitudes of minds effect such things.
They induced into the minds of others whatever they wanted.
The love of commanding sinks the mind into its proprium.
Unless he has an intention to marry her.
His place in the temple agrees with his mind.
Debilitated in mind... because his conceit had been depressed.
The love of uses holds together the mind in its delight. DWis 11. 4.
He rejected the Word from his mind.
In the Spiritual World there is a communication of minds; that is, of thoughts and affections.
All the evil have a mind and cupidity, consequently a will, to destroy the truths of Heaven...
It is in their mind that good works may be omitted.
Eminence and opulence (are what) principally affect minds, because they are proper to the natural man.
They keep the mind as in a prison...
